properties.name: reflow2's code reasons from the declared meanings — every computation that selects relationships by meaning does so through the readings — and every relationship it derives is a declared rule that the code runs or is checked against
properties.source: Anthony, 2026-09-28, in a dev_reflow2 session: "what is applicable to reflow2 and storyflow from the 5 tests? If we need to apply things to reflow2 and storyflow, then please add them to their respective design graphs also." Test 3 of dec:what-a-true-knowledge-graph-is (graph-primitives design on flo2, graph 85a2a1a36e7c942d), accepted on his word the same day.
properties.statement:
Test 3 of the accepted definition of a true knowledge graph (graph-primitives design on flo2: dec:what-a-true-knowledge-graph-is), applied to reflow2.

(1) Every computation that selects relationships by what they MEAN does so through the declared readings, never through a private list of names. req:every-edge-type-declares-what-it-means says a computation CAN select by reading; this says it MUST. Baseline: the projections of dec:a-projection-is-named-and-the-battery-runs-over-it are hand-kept name lists, and exclusion lists are private constants (structure.rs, heal.rs).
(2) Every relationship reflow2 derives from others is declared as a composition of primitives — an inference rule the graph holds. Baseline: 0 of 23 declared (e.g. the contract pair PROVIDES ∘ CONSUMES⁻¹, coupling lifted up part-of, "delivered" = satisfied ∧ built ∧ its check passes, or every part delivered).
(3) Each declared rule is either what the code runs, or checked to give the same result as the code on a real design; a declared rule nothing runs or checks is decoration.

Met when a check passes over every meaning-selecting computation and every derived relationship.
